name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,517

clue.text: A frequent flyer gets caught when returning to African capital

indicators.note: the flyer 'gets' the abbreviation for caught, taking it inside itself
returning means going back the way you came, so the whole string is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
a bird of prey constantly on the wing
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An air-miles traveller is arrested on arriving back in some African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside HAWK just after its first letter, giving A HCAWK, which is then turned round. 'Capital' here means money, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The kwacha is the national currency of Zambia and Malawi, and capital can mean money.

clue.text: Athlete's preparation for heat

blocks.note: first meaning: the stretching and jogging done before an event
second meaning: to make something warmer, as a two-word verb

explanation.surface: A runner limbering up before the first race, the heat, of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' looks like a qualifying race, but it is a verb meaning to make hotter.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the light exercise before sport; the phrasal verb means raise the temperature of something.

clue.text: Mournful song about flower from occupied land, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and listen to what it sounds like

blocks.note: a flower is a crossword river (something that flows), and Crimea is the peninsula occupied by Russia

explanation.surface: A sad ballad about a bloom from a land under foreign occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is a thing that flows. Crimea, annexed by Russia in 2014, gives a Crimean river spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Cry Me a River is a famous torch song of heartbreak, recorded by Julie London and Justin Timberlake among others.

clue.text: Romania is not exactly part of Turkey!

indicators.note: not exactly means not in its precise form, so the letters are loosely rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A geography gaffe: someone insists Romania is not quite a region of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' does double duty in the surface but the fodder needs it: ROMANIA plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor is the historic name for Anatolia, the peninsula that forms most of modern Turkey.

clue.text: A hut in the setter's tree

indicators.note: in places the hut phrase inside the word for the setter's possession

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: belonging to me
a hogan is a traditional Navajo dwelling, a hut of logs and earth

explanation.surface: A little hut stands in the crossword compiler's own tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A HOGAN goes inside MY. The setter is a crossword convention for me or my.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a tropical hardwood tree prized for its reddish timber in furniture making.

clue.text: Game Jonah played in car

indicators.note: played suggests the name is toyed with, its letters jumbled about
in puts the jumbled name inside the vehicle's letters

blocks.note: MG is a British car make
the name rearranged

explanation.surface: Jonah plays a board game while sitting in a car on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: MG, the classic British sports-car marque, wraps the jumbled JONAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahjong is a Chinese tile-based pastime for four players, similar in spirit to rummy.

clue.text: She's moved by English poet

indicators.note: moved means shifted out of place, so the letters change position

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A woman is emotionally moved by the work of an English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English poet' reads as one phrase, but English is only the letter E; the poet is German.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse, the German Nobel laureate, wrote poetry as well as novels such as Steppenwolf.

clue.text: Place to collect cash: A holiday destination in Asia

blocks.note: in Monopoly you collect 200 each time you pass the Go square
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about where to get money out for a trip to Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to collect cash' sounds like a bank machine, but it is the starting square of the board game Monopoly.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small Indian state on the Arabian Sea coast, famous for beaches and tourism.

clue.text: Nurses act unfairly, holding back fruitcakes

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the letters are held within the run of words
back means going the other way, so the concealed letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Nurses treat unfairly the people they look after, keeping fruitcakes from them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfairly' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the hiding place. 'Fruitcakes' looks like food but is slang for eccentrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal slang for people regarded as crazy or wildly eccentric.

clue.text: Lobster has cry if boiled

indicators.note: boiled means tossed about in bubbling water, so the letters are churned up

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lobster lets out a scream if it is dropped into boiling water.
explanation.walkthrough: The old story that lobsters scream in the pot makes the surface vivid; the creature is both definition and part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Crayfish is a name for the spiny or rock lobster as well as the freshwater crustacean.

clue.text: City to fight with the Athenians, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only opening letters are used

blocks.note: to spar is to box or argue
the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A Greek city prepares to go to war alongside Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Historically Sparta fought against Athens, so the surface is apt; 'with' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the ancient Greek city-state in the Peloponnese famed for its warriors.

clue.text: Aussies seen regularly in quiet tourist attraction

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
in places the kept letters inside the word for silence

blocks.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Australian visitors keep spotting each other at a hushed sightseeing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen' is only a joining word; the regular letters come from 'Aussies' alone. To keep mum is British slang for staying silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery of exhibits is one of the classic places visitors and sightseers go.

clue.text: Bully needs some balls to face wild animal

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a large wild mammal

explanation.surface: A thug needs courage to stand up to a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some balls' suggests nerve, but it is a cricket over: six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to domineer or intimidate, as a bully does, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Generates lots of ideas in rush to put on ladies' underwear

indicators.note: putting on a garment means the wearer goes inside it

blocks.note: women's undergarments
taken as written
to storm is to rush violently

explanation.surface: Someone dashes to pull on lingerie in a great hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not the container signal here but letters of its own; 'to put on' is what wraps the garment round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainstorm is to produce many suggestions quickly, often in a group session.

clue.text: Makes new deal to negate Tories' manoeuvring

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving pieces around skilfully, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician strikes a fresh agreement just to cancel out Conservative scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegotiate is to discuss and agree fresh terms for an existing contract or arrangement.

clue.text: A sterling arrangement for percussion

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A first-rate musical score written for the drum section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sterling' reads as excellent, and 'arrangement' as a musical score; both are just letters and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a struck metal instrument found in the orchestra's percussion section.

clue.text: Lout stumbles upon river in French city

indicators.note: stumbles means trips and falls about, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: A drunken yob trips and falls into a river in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upon' means sitting on top, so the jumbled word comes above the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a large city in south-west France on the Garonne, centre of the aerospace industry.

clue.text: Change in philosophy embraced at talk

indicators.note: embraced means held in someone's arms, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a switch to a new belief or faith
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker's change of heart is welcomed at a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' looks like a joining word before talk, but it is the piece that gets embraced.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is an informal spoken exchange between people, a chat or discussion.

clue.text: Stimulates bouts of heavy drinking, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: carouses are drunken revels

explanation.surface: Binge-drinking sessions get the blood up until someone passes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The C is removed from the front of CAROUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to excite or awaken feeling, so it matches stimulates as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Yield to wild decadence without end

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters of the following word are taken out
wild means uncontrolled, so what remains is thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the starting word
these three letters are removed, not the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to wild excess with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without end' looks like an instruction to drop the last letter; instead the letters E, N and D are removed, leaving CADECE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede is to agree or give way to a demand, so it can mean to yield.

clue.text: Gangster gets artwork out of the house

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
a painting done on wet plaster

explanation.surface: A mobster steals a painting and gets it out of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, borrowed from Italian, means outdoors, in the open air.

clue.text: Discreetly conceals rocks

indicators.note: conceals means keeps tucked inside, so the letters sit within the word before it

blocks.note: letters two to six

explanation.surface: Someone quietly hides some stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the mass of loose broken stones on a mountain slope.

clue.text: Spot head of company in informal dress?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in places the letter inside the phrase for casual wear

blocks.note: dress codes saying no tie are informal
the first letter

explanation.surface: Catching sight of the chief executive turning up in casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside NO TIE, between the I and the E. The question mark flags that informal dress is defined by what is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see or become aware of it, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Friend disembowelled duck

indicators.note: disembowelled means its insides removed, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: a playful name for a duck, from the sound it makes

explanation.surface: A gruesome picture of a duck being gutted by a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter C of QUACKER is removed. Capital-F Friend is the Quakers' own name for a member.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, so a Friend is a member of that faith.

clue.text: Caught shy sort of fish

indicators.note: to have caught a remark is to have heard it, so we go by sound

blocks.note: coy means bashful

explanation.surface: A timid fish is hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like angling, or the cricket abbreviation C, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Koi are ornamental Japanese carp, a coloured variety of fish kept in garden ponds.

clue.text: Leaders of Soviet Union left Marx's birthplace with even more passion

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for a comparative adjective; read as 'more passionate'

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letters are taken

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
L is the abbreviation for left
Karl Marx was born in Trier, in western Germany

explanation.surface: Soviet leaders depart from the German town where Marx was born, feeling ever more fervent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultry describes something hot and sensual, so the comparative means hotter and more passionate.

clue.text: Inhabitants of caves adopting one branch of Buddhism

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the caves word takes the other pieces inside

blocks.note: a den is an animal's lair or cave
the Roman numeral for one
Zen is the meditation-based school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Cave dwellers take up a form of Buddhist practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inhabitants of caves' reads as one phrase, but 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Denizens are residents or occupants of a particular place.

clue.text: Girl takes ship to cross part of southern England

indicators.note: takes means receives inside, so the vessel goes into the name

blocks.note: a common girl's name
SS stands for steamship
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A young woman boards a ferry to sail over to the south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb meaning sail over, but it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is a historic county on England's south coast, containing Brighton.
